newsitem.title: POLAND: Animex to put two subsidiaries on bourse.
newsitem.headline: Animex to put two subsidiaries on bourse.

text.p: Polish food trader and producer Animex SA plans to put two of its subsidiaries on the Warsaw bourse next year, the firm's president said on Tuesday.
Witold Pereta told a news conference that the two firms were food producers Ekodrob, in which Animex has a 51-percent stake, and wholly-owned subsidiary Animex-Wielkopolska.
Pereta did not say on which market they would be listed. Animex shares trade on the Warsaw bourse's main floor.
"Our plans beyond 1997 are such that we're going to want to put the majority of our firms, especially our wholly-owned ones, on the bourse," Pereta said. Animex has 13 wholly-owned subsidiaries.
Ekodrob, based in Ilawa, northern Poland, specialises in health food while Animex-Wielkopolska, based near the western city of Poznan, breeds sheep, cattle and produces fodder.
Pereta did not provide the firms' financial data.
Pereta also said Animex had bought from the northwestern Szczecin province a 51-percent stake in meat firm Zaklady Miesne Agryf w Szczecinie for 11 million zlotys.

He said Animex planned to buy three or four more meat firms by the end of next year, including possibly a firm in the western city of Wroclaw, and firms in the towns of Rawa Mazowiecka and Ostroda Morliny from funds in Poland's National Investment Fund (NFI) programme.
Pereta also said Animex plans to earn 15 million zlotys this year after having netted 41.5 million last year, when the firm received large tax refunds.
